knife_edge_track — DRIVE cutting op

• Data kinds: rgb → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.knife_edge_track(image, board_row: 'float | None' = None, win: 'int' = 6, reject_px: 'float' = 1.0, method: 'str' = 'coverage') -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import cutting; cutting.knife_edge_track(image, board_row: 'float | None' = None, win: 'int' = 6, reject_px: 'float' = 1.0, method: 'str' = 'coverage') -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("knife_edge_track"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Extracts the cutting-edge line, the spine and the tip from the face-view image (rule-based only).

Procedure: per column, pick the row where the vertical luminance step goes "dark → bright" (blade → wall) → exclude food columns (saturation rule) and 3 px around them → refine to sub-pixel by the coverage method (window widened to match the blur estimate) → total-least-squares line (same formulation as measure.fit_line) → drop residuals > reject_px and refit. The upper boundary (spine and the oblique line at the tip) is picked the same way; the continuous part on the right that departs from the spine line = the oblique line, and its intersection with the edge line = the tip. For columns hidden by the food (occluded_cols), the edge is the interpolation of a single line fitted from both sides.

method: "coverage" (default) or "gradient" (centroid of the derivative, for comparison). Returns: angle_deg (counter-clockwise with x right and z up, atan2), line (total least squares of row = cy + (col − cx)·dy/dx), slope, offset, tip_rc (tip; None if not found), n_points, rms_px, cols_used, occluded_cols. ValueError if no blade is visible.
